output.summary: Deterministic policy_verdict is NO_VERDICT with analysis coverage INCOMPLETE (reasons RESOURCE_GAPS and MISSING_RESOURCE_CELLS). The two evaluated workload windows differ: workload-03 has business_verdict PASS (response_time_p95 53 ms <= 200) but resource_verdict NO_VERDICT because the database-limit check on db_work returned NO_VERDICT with reason MISSING_RESOURCE_CELLS (1 missing cell); workload-04 has window verdict FAIL with response_time_p95 28815 ms (> 200), cpu_work mean 0.99998/max 1, and target rate ~110 requests/s. The compute-limit SLA rule on cpu_work FAILED in both windows. No correlation headline was selected: pairs are BELOW_EFFECT or INSUFFICIENT_DATA, all uncertainty NOT_ESTIMATED, and clock_alignment is not_verified_by_core, so no causal or lead/lag claim is supported. error_count was 0 in every metric; that does not indicate spare capacity or stability.

hypotheses.observation: Workload-04 policy check observed response_time_p95 28815 ms vs threshold 200 ms (FAIL); window-metric p95 28815 / p50 15231 / max 30323; window cpu_work mean 0.99998 with max 1 and min 0.992899; generator target rate ~110 requests/s.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The latency failure co-occurs in the same window with CPU near 1.0 and a higher applied rate than workload-03 (110 vs 90 requests/s), which is consistent with saturation/queuing, but this is only a hypothesis: the CPU-vs-latency correlation pair for this window is INSUFFICIENT_DATA (NO_RESIDUAL_VARIATION, lag_used_cells 0) and cannot confirm it.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Inspect the interval series for cpu_work and latency across workload-04 to identify the first elevated latency cell, then rerun with controlled load variation so an association estimate can be computed.

hypotheses.observation: Workload-03 window has business_verdict PASS but resource_verdict NO_VERDICT and overall verdict NO_VERDICT; the database-limit policy check on db_work is NO_VERDICT with reason MISSING_RESOURCE_CELLS; the db_work series has 1 missing cell and longest_gap_cells 1 with reasons RESOURCE_GAPS; analysis coverage is INCOMPLETE.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The db_work SLA policy could not be evaluated because a telemetry cell was missing, so the window resource verdict and the overall policy verdict stayed NO_VERDICT rather than PASS; a missing cell is a data completeness limitation, not evidence that the window was healthy.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Rerun workload-03 (or the full scenario) after ensuring gap-free db_work telemetry so the product can evaluate the database-limit rule and produce a resource verdict for the window.

hypotheses.observation: Correlation pairs for cpu_work and db_work vs response_time_p95_ms are BELOW_EFFECT in workload-03 (raw_rho 0.446860 and 0.105728) or INSUFFICIENT_DATA in workload-04 (raw_rho 0.099834 with lag_used_cells 0); in workload-03 the target-rate control was dropped because it was constant at 90; all uncertainty is NOT_ESTIMATED; headline selections are UNAVAILABLE with MULTI_WINDOW_FAMILY_UNSUPPORTED and, for workload-04, GENUINE_PARTIAL_UNCALIBRATED.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: Constant load inside workload-03 (target rate 90) and flat, saturated CPU in workload-04 left too little variation for the correlation machinery, and the multi-window family selection is unsupported, so the analysis could not establish an association; this does not prove CPU is unrelated to latency.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Rerun with in-window load variation and an analysis family the tool can evaluate (single-window) so a calibrated association estimate and headline can be produced.

hypotheses.observation: Correlation pairs report best_lag values (e.g., -6000 ms for db_work in workload-03, -10000 ms in workload-04) and lag profiles, while the resource binding states clock_alignment not_verified_by_core.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: Without clock verification, apparent lags between resource and latency series cannot be read as duration offsets or as ordering between series; raw epoch positions do not by themselves establish which series leads.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Verify clock alignment between generator and system telemetry before interpreting any lag; treat all best_lag values as unverified until clocks are aligned.

hypotheses.observation: error_count is 0 in the overall metric, the per-transaction metric, and both window metric summaries, and the diagnostic summary reports anomalies_tested 0 and episodes_reported 0, while response_time_p95 reached 28815 ms in workload-04.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: Absence of recorded sampler errors and reported anomaly episodes does not imply stability or spare capacity; a severe latency policy failure occurred with zero errors, so error counts cannot rule out a capacity problem.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Inspect the per-cell latency distribution and resource series over workload-04, and rerun with a healthy generator if needed, rather than treating 0 errors as a clean bill of health.

recommendations.action: Rerun the scenario after fixing telemetry gaps so the db_work series in workload-03 has no missing cells, allowing the database-limit SLA rule to be evaluated and a resource verdict for that window to be produced.
recommendations.rationale: The overall policy_verdict is NO_VERDICT and coverage is INCOMPLETE because db_work had 1 missing cell (RESOURCE_GAPS) and the database-limit check returned NO_VERDICT (MISSING_RESOURCE_CELLS) in workload-03; NO_VERDICT is not PASS and can only be resolved by data the product can evaluate.

recommendations.action: Inspect the workload-04 transition in the interval series (target rate ~110 vs ~90 requests/s, cpu_work mean 0.99998/max 1, latency p95 28815 ms) to determine where the latency increase begins.
recommendations.rationale: The correlation pair for workload-04 could not confirm an association (INSUFFICIENT_DATA, NO_RESIDUAL_VARIATION) and clock alignment is not_verified_by_core, so direct inspection of the series is the bounded next step; zero recorded errors do not prove capacity stability.

recommendations.action: Verify clock alignment between generator and system telemetry before asserting any lead/lag between load, CPU, and latency.
recommendations.rationale: resource_binding reports clock_alignment not_verified_by_core, and correlation pairs report best_lag values that cannot be interpreted as temporal ordering until clocks are verified.

recommendations.action: Rerun with load variation inside each window (rather than a constant 90 requests/s in workload-03 and flat CPU near 1.0 in workload-04) and keep the analysis within a family the tool can evaluate, so the correlation machinery can produce an effect estimate.
recommendations.rationale: Pairs were BELOW_EFFECT or INSUFFICIENT_DATA with reasons CONSTANT_CONTROL, NO_RESIDUAL_VARIATION, RESOURCE_DELTA_BELOW_MINIMUM, and headline selection was UNAVAILABLE with MULTI_WINDOW_FAMILY_UNSUPPORTED; without variation no association or capacity insight could be estimated.

caveats: The deterministic policy_verdict is NO_VERDICT and analysis coverage is INCOMPLETE (RESOURCE_GAPS, MISSING_RESOURCE_CELLS); workload-04 is FAIL and workload-03 is NO_VERDICT. This advice does not modify that verdict.
The db_work NO_VERDICT (MISSING_RESOURCE_CELLS) is not PASS and not FAIL; a missing resource cell must not be interpreted as a healthy value or as policy compliance.
Correlation uncertainty is NOT_ESTIMATED for all pairs, no headline was selected, and reported raw/partial rho values are not calibrated significance; do not treat them as proven effect sizes.
clock_alignment is not_verified_by_core, so no lead/lag ordering or temporal causal claim is supported by the evidence; recommend clock verification before any time-ordering interpretation.
Counts are scoped differently: overall sample_count 93000 vs window sample_counts 27000 and 33000 cover different scopes/windows; these are not inconsistent and should not be combined directly.
error_count 0 and anomalies_tested 0 do not demonstrate stability, spare capacity, or absence of a capacity problem; the p95 latency policy failure in workload-04 occurred with zero recorded errors.
No capacity bound or knee result is present in this evidence; no statement about capacity bounds or knee detectors is made here.
run_validity is VALID but that refers to run acceptance, not to completeness of resource coverage or policy evaluation in the windows.
